clue.text: But one may not be at sea in one's varying choices

definitions.text: But one may not be at sea in one's varying choices

parts.words: But one may not be at sea in one's varying choices
parts.note: someone afloat is normally at sea, but this kind of voter drifts between parties at the polls without ever being on the water

explanation.surface: A wry remark about someone who changes their mind often yet never leaves dry land.
explanation.definitionFit: An elector with no fixed party loyalty, whose vote may go either way, is said to drift like something on the tide.

clue.text: A dress-conscious trendy has it on as if at random

indicators.note: letters put together at random are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone who follows fashion wears something as if casually chosen.
explanation.definitionFit: A person devoted to following the latest styles in clothing is a modern label for a fashion follower.

clue.text: Only initially long to express a view

indicators.note: initially asks for just the opening letter of the word Only

parts.note: to long for something is to pine for it

explanation.surface: Advice that one should only briefly yearn to state an opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: To state an opinion or give one's thoughts is a formal verb meaning to voice a judgment.

clue.text: Got up to lag water source in absorbent material

indicators.note: to lag is to wrap something round, so one piece encloses the others
in a down clue, up means the word Got is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned
a well is a source of water
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stood up to insulate a water source with a spongy fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got up' reads as stood up; 'up' reverses it to TOG, and 'to lag' (wrap, as pipes are lagged) puts the water source and 'in' inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Terry cloth used for bath sheets is a soft fabric that soaks up water, a looped cotton cloth.

clue.text: Granny going round initially in honour of weepy daughter

indicators.note: going round means the grandmother encircles the other pieces

parts.note: nan is an informal word for grandmother

indicators.note: initially takes only the opening letter of the word in

parts.note: the OBE (Order of the British Empire) is a British honour

explanation.surface: Grandmother is fussing around a tearful girl in tribute to her.
explanation.walkthrough: Niobe, daughter of Tantalus in Greek myth, wept endlessly for her slain children and was turned to stone still weeping.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things pertaining to Niobe, the mythical mother famous for ceaseless tears.

clue.text: Quick to change right to view leader's flat?

indicators.note: to change one letter to another means swapping the abbreviation for right for a new letter

parts.note: rapid means quick

indicators.note: leader's points to the opening letter of the word view

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a leader's apartment can be fixed swiftly so the view improves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat?' looks like a home tied to the view; it means dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Something insipid, dull and lacking liveliness is described as flat in tone or flavour.

clue.text: Insect resorted to this mostly, swallowing bug

indicators.note: swallowing means the rearranged letters take the bug inside them
resorted read as re-sorted means sorted again, so letters are rearranged
mostly means all but the last letter of the word this is used

parts.note: a bug is an informal word for a germ

explanation.surface: Someone fell back on this approach, though it largely took in a fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resorted' reads as 'fell back on' but means re-sorted: 'mostly' trims this to THI, the shuffle gives TIOTH, and 'swallowing' takes the bug inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A brightly patterned moth of the family Arctiidae is a kind of insect, also the name of a biplane.

clue.text: Aussie native requiring a lot of space

indicators.note: a lot of, but not all, so the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: room means space

explanation.surface: An Australian creature that needs plenty of room to move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' takes ROOM without its last letter M.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for kangaroo, the marsupial is a well-known animal native to Australia.

clue.text: Sparkling wine son dipped into shortly after midday

indicators.note: dipped into means the son goes inside the time phrase

parts.note: shortly after midday is at one o'clock, at I with I as the Roman numeral one
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A boy sips a bubbly drink just after noon.
explanation.walkthrough: One o'clock is shortly after midday, so read 'at one' as AT I.
explanation.definitionFit: A fizzy white from Piedmont in northern Italy is a well-known spumante, a bubbly Italian drink.

clue.text: Club taking responsibility for a ravager of crops?

parts.note: a wood is a type of golf club
'not my pigeon' means not my responsibility

explanation.surface: A club takes charge of dealing with whatever is destroying farmers' fields.
explanation.walkthrough: PIGEON for responsibility is a British idiom: 'that's not my pigeon' means not my concern.
explanation.definitionFit: This large dove is a notorious farm pest, feeding heavily on cereals and brassicas in fields.

clue.text: Beauty in fiction a victim of defamation

indicators.note: in places the beauty inside the word for fiction

parts.note: a lie is a fiction, an untruth
a belle is a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: A beautiful character in a novel suffers from slander.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, the person about whom a libel is published is the injured party in a defamation case.

clue.text: Gain enjoyment at first in outing

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the word for an outing

parts.note: a drive is an outing in a car

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word enjoyment

explanation.surface: Get pleasure early on during a trip out.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain or draw something, such as benefit or income, from a source is to get it.

clue.text: Defence of very popular article, in a manner of speaking

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable

indicators.note: in puts the article inside the word for a manner of speaking

parts.note: diction is one's manner of speaking
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A justification of a well-liked grammar item, phrased in a certain way of talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a manner of speaking' reads as a stock phrase; here 'in' is the insertion signal and 'a manner of speaking' is DICTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Justification or support of a position against criticism amounts to a defence of it.

clue.text: Remove right from subscribers? It's not intended

indicators.note: remove says a letter is taken out of the word for subscribers

parts.note: the undersigned are those who subscribe (sign) a document

explanation.surface: An instruction to strike a right off the list of members, which turns out to be accidental.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subscribers' suggests magazine readers; here it means those who sign their names below a document.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unplanned or accidental, done without design or purpose, was not deliberate.

clue.text: Copying letter in Greek and Latin, for one outside

indicators.note: outside means the abbreviation for 'for one' wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: eg (for example) is a way of saying 'for one'
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A student transcribing a character in Greek and Latin, perhaps sitting outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for one' is EG, which goes 'outside' MU and LATIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Imitating someone, trying to match or equal them, is a form of following their example.

clue.text: In which we may be on track for taking certain courses

definitions.text: In which we may be on track for taking certain courses

parts.words: In which we may be on track for taking certain courses
parts.note: courses suggest study and on track suggests progress, but the scene is a meal of several courses eaten aboard a train

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a student keeping up with a study programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway carriage where passengers are served meals of starter, main and dessert while travelling.

clue.text: Noise from Tamworth pub largely repressed by fine?

indicators.note: repressed by means held down inside the word for fine

parts.note: OK means fine

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, so the final letter of the synonym goes

parts.note: an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A racket from a bar in the Staffordshire town of Tamworth is muffled by a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: Tamworth is a town but also a British breed of pig; 'largely' cuts INN to IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The grunting sound a pig makes, and a Tamworth is a ginger-coloured breed of pig.

clue.text: Isaacson's appeal accepted in Brussels?

definitions.note: read as Isaac son is, with the definition followed by is

indicators.note: accepted in means the appeal is taken inside the abbreviation for Brussels

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the EU (European Union)
SA is short for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Someone named Isaacson has a legal appeal heard in the Belgian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Isaacson' looks like a surname; read it as Isaac's son. Esau was the elder son of Isaac in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, the hairy elder twin of Jacob was born to Isaac and Rebecca.

clue.text: Finally completing duet, he's in surprisingly good health

indicators.note: finally takes only the closing letter of the word completing
surprisingly signals the letters turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A singer, having finished a duet, is unexpectedly in fine fettle.
explanation.definitionFit: A German word, literally health, said after someone sneezes or as a toast wishing well-being.

clue.text: Little boy's upset stomach leading to bed

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the words are turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: Art, short for Arthur, is a little boy's name, so Art's
tum is an informal word for stomach

explanation.surface: A small child's tummy upset sends him off to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' is a geological layer, not a place to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer of rock or soil in geology is a bed or seam.

clue.text: Slag off a close relative, an exporter of bananas and pineapples

definitions.text: an exporter of bananas and pineapples

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly, to slag off
ma (mother) is a close relative

explanation.surface: Someone insults a family member who ships out tropical fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slag off' is British slang for criticise harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Central American republic famous for its canal ships tropical fruit overseas.

clue.text: Friend has a turn crossing busy road

indicators.note: crossing means the pieces span over the road, placed either side of it

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game
the M1 is a busy British motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: A pal takes a moment to walk across a heavily trafficked street.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; crosswords write its 1 as I.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish word for a male chum, borrowed into English as a word for a pal.

clue.text: Contact staff about centre for heart bypass

parts.note: to ring someone is to contact them by phone

indicators.note: about means the staff goes round the middle letter

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick

indicators.note: centre for takes the middle letter of the word heart

explanation.surface: A hospital phones its staff about a cardiac bypass operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart bypass' reads as surgery; the definition is 'bypass' alone, a road skirting a town.
explanation.definitionFit: A road circling a town centre so traffic can avoid it is a bypass.

clue.text: Souvenir from Long Island found in park

indicators.note: found in means the island abbreviation sits inside the park word

parts.note: the rec (recreation ground) is a British word for a park

explanation.surface: A memento from a New York island turns up in a park.
explanation.walkthrough: The rec, short for recreation ground, is a British public park or playing field.
explanation.definitionFit: An object kept from the past as a reminder or memento can be called a keepsake.

clue.text: Hopeful fellow is taken in by viewer

indicators.note: taken in by means these pieces go inside the viewer word

parts.note: an optic is an eye or lens, a viewer
Tim is a man's name, a fellow

explanation.surface: An expectant chap is fooled by someone watching.
explanation.definitionFit: Expecting a good outcome and looking on the bright side are marks of a positive outlook.

clue.text: Pulse rate finally disturbing old man

indicators.note: disturbing means the letter breaks into the word for old man

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word rate

explanation.surface: An elderly man's heartbeat is racing, which is alarming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' is not a heartbeat here: it is an edible seed of a legume.
explanation.definitionFit: Edible seeds of legumes such as lentils and beans are classed as pulses.

clue.text: Rested in country road, when picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: a lane is a narrow country road

explanation.surface: Someone took a rest in a rural lane after being given a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: The past participle of lie, as in having reclined or stayed at rest.

clue.text: Like certain relations cooking an organic meal?

indicators.note: cooking means the letters are being worked into something new

explanation.surface: Asks whether preparing a wholesome dinner resembles family ties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relations' suggests family; it means ties between Britain and the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Ties between Britain and the United States are described with this compound adjective.
